title: Shadow Experiments (Console) — UI copy + tooltips (draft)
body:
NOTE: Draft copy for Console. Expect iteration after dogfood + security review. Keep tone: precise, non-alarmist, clear about “no user impact” and “stats are noisy”.

==========
1) NAV + PAGE TITLES
==========
Left nav item:
- “Shadow experiments”

Shadow experiments list page:
- Title: “Shadow experiments”
- Subtitle: “Compare candidate variants against production responses using mirrored traffic and asynchronous scoring.”

Create flow:
- Step title: “Create shadow experiment”
- Step subtitle (optional): “Mirror a sampled subset of requests to one or more shadow variants. Users continue to receive the control response.”

Experiment details page:
- Title: “Shadow experiment: {experiment_name}”
- Status pill values: “Draft”, “Running”, “Paused”, “Stopped”, “Completed”

==========
2) HIGH-LEVEL EXPLAINERS (INFO BANNERS)
==========
Banner (top of create page):
- Heading: “What is shadow traffic?”
- Body: “Shadow traffic duplicates a sample of real production requests to one or more candidate variants. We return the control response to the user and score shadow outputs asynchronously to measure quality deltas.”
- Link text: “Learn how scoring and retention work”

Banner (visible when editing sampling or targets):
- Heading: “Shadowing is fail-open”
- Body: “If the shadow path is unhealthy (timeouts, backpressure, scoring lag), the user path remains unaffected. Your experiment may show reduced sample size during degraded periods.”

Banner (safety / cost warning shown when sampling > X% or adding multiple targets):
- Heading: “Sampling and targets increase cost”
- Body: “Each shadow target generates additional tokens and scoring work. Start small (e.g., 0.1%–1%) and ramp up after confirming overhead and statistical stability.”

Banner (privacy / data handling):
- Heading: “Data minimization and retention”
- Body: “Shadow artifacts may include prompt/response fragments needed for scoring. Redwood applies redaction and short retention by default. Dedicated/Private tenants may configure stricter retention or opt out of storing examples.”

==========
3) CREATE EXPERIMENT — FIELD LABELS + HELP TEXT
==========
Section header:
- “Baseline”
- Helper: “The baseline (control) is the user-visible route configuration. Shadow variants are compared against the control response.”

Field: Route
- Label: “Route”
- Placeholder: “Select a route”
- Help text: “The production route whose requests will be sampled for shadowing.”
- Tooltip: “Shadowing attaches to a route, not a single model. If your route uses fallbacks or regional routing, the control response may vary by policy.”

Field: Control variant
- Label: “Control”
- Value display: “Current route config (user response)”
- Tooltip: “Users always receive the control response. Control responses are still recorded for comparison and scoring context.”

Section header:
- “Shadow targets”
- Helper: “Shadow targets receive mirrored requests and are scored asynchronously. You can add multiple targets to compare several candidates at once.”

Field: Add target button
- Button: “Add shadow target”

Per target fields:
- Label: “Target name” (placeholder: “e.g., Llama-3.1-70B-q4 (candidate)”) 
- Label: “Variant type” (dropdown values): “Model version”, “Quantization profile”, “Prompt template”, “Routing policy”
- Label: “Target” (placeholder: “Select model/version or config”) 
- Label: “Max shadow timeout”
  - Help text: “Shadow requests time out independently and never block the user response.”
  - Tooltip: “Shorter timeouts reduce overhead but may bias results toward shorter outputs or faster paths.”

Section header:
- “Sampling”

Field: Sampling rate
- Label: “Sampling rate”
- Help text: “Percent of production requests mirrored to shadow targets.”
- Tooltip: “Sampling is deterministic per request fingerprint to reduce variance over time. The same request pattern tends to be consistently included/excluded across the experiment.”
- Inline guidance (beneath slider/input):
  - “Recommended start: 0.1%–1%”
  - “For stable deltas, aim for at least {N} scored pairs per metric.”

Field: Eligibility filters (optional)
- Label: “Filters (optional)”
- Placeholder: “Add filters (request type, route tag, region, etc.)”
- Help text: “Restrict shadowing to a subset of traffic. Filters are applied before sampling.”
- Tooltip: “Avoid high-cardinality filters (e.g., user_id). Filters can reduce sample size and slow time-to-signal.”

Section header:
- “Scoring and metrics”

Field: Metric bundle
- Label: “Metric bundle”
- Dropdown options (v1 examples):
  - “Default (v1): safety + format + instruction following”
  - “Format-only (fast)”
  - “Safety-only”
- Tooltip: “Metrics are computed asynchronously from shadow outputs and may lag traffic by several minutes. Some metrics use model-graded scoring and can introduce variance.”

Field: Rubric version
- Label: “Rubric version”
- Default value text: “Latest stable”
- Tooltip: “Pin a rubric version to make results comparable over time. Changing the rubric changes what ‘good’ means.”

Field: Store examples
- Label: “Store example requests/responses”
- Toggle help text: “Enables example drilldown. Redaction and retention policies apply.”
- Tooltip: “Disabling examples reduces stored content but also limits debugging. Aggregates and metrics remain available.”

CTA buttons:
- Primary: “Start experiment”
- Secondary: “Save draft”
- Tertiary: “Cancel”

Start experiment confirmation modal:
- Title: “Start shadow experiment?”
- Body: “We’ll begin mirroring {sampling_rate}% of requests from {route} to {num_targets} shadow target(s). Users will continue to receive control responses.”
- Cost note: “Estimated incremental tokens: {estimate} / day (based on last 24h traffic).”
- Buttons: “Start”, “Cancel”

==========
4) LIST PAGE — EMPTY STATES + TABLE COPY
==========
Empty state (no experiments):
- Title: “Measure quality changes without user impact”
- Body: “Shadow experiments mirror a sample of production requests to candidate variants and score outputs asynchronously. Use them to catch regressions before changing user-visible routing.”
- Primary CTA: “Create shadow experiment”
- Secondary link: “Read best practices”

Table column headers:
- “Name”
- “Route”
- “Status”
- “Sampling”
- “Targets”
- “Last signal”
- “Created by”

Table row status helper text (hover):
- Draft: “Not receiving traffic.”
- Running: “Mirroring traffic and scoring results.”
- Paused: “Mirroring paused; scoring may continue for queued items.”
- Stopped: “Mirroring stopped; results remain available.”

==========
5) RESULTS PAGE — HEADERS, METRIC CARDS, AND CHART TOOLTIPS
==========
Top summary panel labels:
- “Control: {control_description}”
- “Shadow target: {target_name}” (if multiple targets, this is a selector)
- “Sampling: {sampling_rate}%”
- “Time window: {window_selector}”

Callout when scoring lag is present:
- Banner heading: “Scoring is delayed”
- Body: “Results reflect traffic up to {last_scored_timestamp}. Current lag: {lag_minutes} minutes. If lag persists, reduce sampling or check pipeline health.”

Metric card format (example copy):
- Card title: “Format adherence”
- Subtext: “Share of responses matching the required schema.”
- Value line: “Delta vs control: {delta}”
- Secondary line: “95% CI: [{low}, {high}]”
- Footnote: “Based on {n} scored pairs.”

Metric tooltip (delta definition):
- “Delta is computed as (shadow − control) over matched request pairs in the selected time window. Positive delta may be better or worse depending on the metric.”

Tooltip (confidence interval):
- “Confidence intervals reflect sampling variability. If the interval crosses 0, the true delta may be near zero. Small sample sizes and heavy-tailed outcomes widen intervals.”

Tooltip (matched pairs):
- “We score control and shadow outputs for the same request fingerprint when available. If one side times out or is dropped, the pair may be excluded from that metric.”

Tooltip (interpretation guidance shown near top of page):
- “How to read results”
  - “Look for consistent deltas across time and segments.”
  - “Prioritize large, statistically stable regressions before acting.”
  - “A ‘no change detected’ result may mean low sample size.”

Delta chart axis label copy:
- Y-axis: “Delta vs control”
- X-axis: “Time”

Chart hover tooltip template:
- “Time: {timestamp}”
- “Delta: {delta}”
- “95% CI: [{low}, {high}]”
- “Scored pairs: {n}”
- “Dropped (timeout/filtered): {dropped_count}”

Segment filter label:
- “Break down by”
- Options (examples): “None”, “Region”, “Request type”, “Model fallback path”, “Route tag”
- Segment tooltip: “Segments may reduce sample size. High-cardinality segmentation is limited to protect system health.”

Examples drilldown section:
- Header: “Examples (redacted)”
- Subheader: “Inspect a small sample to understand why metrics changed.”

Examples empty state (examples disabled or retention too strict):
- Title: “Examples unavailable”
- Body (option A - disabled): “This experiment was created with example storage disabled.”
- Body (option B - retention/redaction): “Examples are not stored for this tenant configuration. Aggregates are still available.”
- Link: “View data handling settings”

==========
6) WARNINGS / GUARDRAILS (INLINE COPY)
==========
Warning when adding >1 shadow target:
- “Multiple shadow targets increase incremental token usage and scoring load. Consider running separate experiments if you need clearer attribution.”

Warning when sampling is high:
- “High sampling can increase downstream cost and may trigger shadow backpressure. If backpressure activates, results may be incomplete.”

Warning for streaming routes:
- “Streaming requests may capture partial outputs for scoring when the shadow path times out. Metrics may skew if partials are frequent.”

Warning for tool/function calling (if applicable in UI):
- “If your route uses tool calls, shadow variants may call different tools or produce different arguments. Shadowing does not execute external side effects on behalf of the user.”

Tooltip for “fail-open”/circuit breaker state:
- “Shadowing is temporarily reduced or disabled to protect the user path. Metrics during this period may have reduced sample size.”

==========
7) COMMON ERROR / DEGRADED MODE MESSAGES
==========
Create experiment validation errors:
- “Sampling rate must be between 0 and 10.”
- “At least one shadow target is required.”
- “This route is not eligible for shadow experiments (unsupported request type).”
- “Selected metric bundle requires example storage to be enabled.” (only if true)

Start experiment error toast:
- “Couldn’t start experiment. No changes were applied.”
- Secondary: “Try again or contact support if the issue persists.”

Permissions/RBAC:
- Page-level empty permission state:
  - Title: “You don’t have access to shadow experiments”
  - Body: “Ask an admin for the Shadow Experiments: Read permission.”
- Create disabled tooltip:
  - “You need Shadow Experiments: Write permission to create or edit experiments.”

Scoring unavailable:
- Banner heading: “Scoring is unavailable”
- Body: “Traffic mirroring may continue, but metrics won’t update until scoring recovers. Check status page or reduce sampling.”

Telemetry lag:
- Banner heading: “Telemetry is delayed”
- Body: “Results may be incomplete for the most recent window. Last ingested: {timestamp}.”

==========
8) ROLLOUTS INTEGRATION COPY (ATTACH TO CANARY/A-B)
==========
Rollout sidebar widget title:
- “Shadow quality signals”

Widget body (when attached):
- “This rollout is linked to shadow experiment {experiment_name}. Quality deltas are advisory and do not change traffic by themselves.”

Widget body (when not attached):
- “No shadow experiment linked. Link an experiment to monitor quality deltas during rollout.”
- CTA: “Link shadow experiment”

Tooltip (advisory vs automatic):
- “At launch, quality signals are advisory. Use them to inform manual rollback decisions.”

Rollout timeline event text:
- “Shadow experiment started (sampling {sampling_rate}%).”
- “Shadow experiment paused.”
- “Shadow experiment stopped.”

==========
9) BEST PRACTICES / EDUCATIONAL MICROCOPY (OPTIONAL PANEL)
==========
Panel title: “Best practices”
Panel bullets:
- “Start with a small sampling rate and one target.”
- “Run long enough to capture typical traffic variation (peak/off-peak, weekdays/weekends).”
- “Validate segment-specific regressions (e.g., specific regions or request types).”
- “Use examples to interpret metric movement, not as a substitute for statistical confidence.”
- “If deltas are unstable, increase sample size or narrow scope with filters.”

==========
10) OPEN QUESTIONS (FOR REVIEW)
==========
- Do we explicitly say ‘model-graded scoring may disagree with humans’? (Applied ML wants a gentle caveat; PM wants it short.)
- “Positive delta = good/bad” varies per metric. Should each metric card show a small “higher is better” indicator text (no icons yet)?
- What’s the default recommended sampling in UI for Hosted vs Dedicated? SRE suggested different caps.
- How do we phrase ‘examples are redacted’ without implying we catch all sensitive content? Legal/security review needed.

END
